title: Garden Centre
strapline: Everything growing needs a little care.
intent: A garden centre blends shop play with real growing, so children serve customers and care for living things.
Watering, potting and tending plants builds care, patience and a first understanding of what living things need.
The shop side brings counting, money and sorting — plants by size, by colour, by price.
Digging, pouring, potting and carrying stretch physical control and strength.
Rich talk grows here — seeds, roots, soil, bulbs, watering can, wheelbarrow — alongside real questions about how things grow.
implementation: Set up a shop counter and a 'growing' area with pots, compost or gravel, seeds or artificial plants, and watering cans.
Take a customer or new-gardener role so children advise, serve and care for the plants.
Model the care talk: 'This one looks thirsty — what does it need? Where should it go to get some sun?'
Bring in real number and sorting: prices, how many pots, sort the tall plants from the small.
Add labels, a plant-care sign and a till so writing, reading and counting all have a purpose.
Wherever possible, grow something real alongside — cress, beans, bulbs — so the play connects to living change.
Follow children who love digging and pouring, and let the potting bench be the heart of it.
key_questions: What does a plant need to grow big and strong?
How can you tell this plant is thirsty?
How many pots does this customer need, and how much will they cost?
How could we sort these plants so customers can find them?
What will you write on the label so we know what's growing?

impact.text: Children care for plants — watering, potting, placing them in the light — and talk about what growing things need.
Children serve customers and advise them in role, holding real conversations about the plants.
Children sort and group the plants by size, colour or kind and explain how they've arranged them.
Children count pots, seeds and coins and handle prices at the till.
Children dig, pour, pot and carry with growing physical control and strength.
Children make labels and signs and read them back, mark-making with meaning.

enhancements: A potting bench with compost or gravel, pots, trowels and seed packets.
Real seeds or bulbs to plant and watch over the following weeks.
Watering cans, a wheelbarrow and gardening gloves.
A till, coins, plant labels and price signs.
Sorting trays or shelves labelled by size or colour.
A 'plant hospital' corner for reviving droopy plants.

playing_exploring: Children play at a real, familiar place and get their hands genuinely dirty exploring soil and seeds.
They test what pouring, digging and potting can do.
active_learning: Children stay with the slow care of growing things, coming back to check and water over days.
creating_thinking: Children work out what each plant needs, how to sort the stock, and how to solve a customer's request.
